correctness.rationale: Tang–Fan Theorem 1.2/Table 1 specializes at r=1 (including q=3) to s=(-a)^h=-1 or 3 for a nonzero; the latter disappears in characteristic 3. The exponent map has kernel h and its image contains the base multiplicative group; a=0 independently gives the gcd(3,q+1) test. The nonzero fixed points are a fiber over u=1-a of the map with image μ_h and kernel 2(q−1). In the s=-1 branch, the two norm-one requirements give Tr(a)=1 and u=a inverse, so a^h=1 but h must be odd and a^3=-1. In the s=3 branch the two norm requirements give u²+7u+1=0. In characteristic 5 its root -1 fails u^h=1; in other eligible characteristics split roots in the base field cannot be ±1. For nonsquare 5 the roots -φ^{±4} satisfy u^h=(-1)^h, and for h even the coefficient test reduces to (-a)^h=-3χ_q(3). Quadratic reciprocity, restriction of characters from the prime subfield at odd extension degree, and q≡3 mod 4 give exactly 7 and 43 mod 60. Thus the histogram including the degenerate coefficient follows.
residual_risks: The packaged diagnostic prescreens coefficients by the theorem, then tests the admitted maps; it is not an independent check of necessity. My replay checks every coefficient without the criterion for q=3,5,7,9,11,13,25,27,49,81,125 and all possible high-fixed-point coefficients at q=343, on the q+1 multiplicative fibers. No finite replay proves the general classification.

value.rationale: The fixed-point count is a natural first dynamical invariant of this classified family. Knowing exactly when nonzero parameters yield 2q−1 rather than one fixed point, with explicit parameters, gives a uniform selection rule across prime powers rather than an isolated small-field check. The exact mod-60 boundary is not supplied by the known permutation classification.
